title: Fragment affinity prober and SSE hedging policy
creator: Ava Patel
description: Users intermittently observe truncated streaming responses after client reconnects or rapid network flaps. Current resume token design recovers content but can cause duplicate fragments or tool/function-call boundary violations when the server returns partial deltas. This ticket implements two complementary mechanisms: a runtime-side affinity prober to mark fragment lineage and a conservative hedging policy that launches a warm standby stream for short reconnect windows. The goal is to reduce visible duplication and preserve function-call and structured-output boundaries while keeping tail latency stable.
design_decision: We will add a lightweight per-session fragment affinity tag (opaque short hash) attached to each emitted chunk and checkpoint. Clients rejoining include the last-seen affinity tag; servers use it to verify fragment lineage. For brief disconnects (<3s) we will enable hedged warm reconnects: client may open a speculative secondary connection; server will mark speculatively emitted fragments with 'hedge' provenance and suppress duplicates during final reconciliation. Hedging is opt-in per-route and bounded by token-window and server concurrency limits.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces visible duplication and boundary-splitting for function calls; improves perceived reliability on flaky networks. Cons: introduces modest extra state and metadata on fragments, increases server-side ephemeral work for hedged streams, and may slightly increase token egress during hedging windows. We keep hedging off by default and require route opt-in to limit cost impact.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime attaches 8-char affinity tag to each chunk and checkpoint metadata
Reconnect handshake accepts last-seen affinity tag and validates lineage to avoid re-emitting identical fragments
Hedging policy available as per-route flag with default disabled
End-to-end tests show >90% reduction in duplicated tool/function-call frames for simulated 500ms intermittent network drop scenarios
Latency p50/p95 regressions during hedging remain within 5% in synthetic workload
Documentation and client SDK guidance published
steps: 1) Add affinity tag generation in serving runtime chunk emitter (C++): 8-byte TruncatedSHA1 of parent checkpoint + seq
2) Embed affinity tag in SSE 'data' envelope as metadata header field and in resume checkpoint records
3) Update resume handshake flow to accept optional 'Last-Affinity' header and validate on server-side before re-emitting overlapping segments
4) Implement hedging controller that can spawn speculative replica streams tied to session id with hedgingTTL and tokenBudget guards
5) Expose route config and console toggle for hedging with defaults and cost warnings
6) Add client SDK guidance for enabling warm reconnects and how to surface hedged fragments for reconciliation
7) Add comprehensive integration tests and load tests; deploy to canary subset of hosted runtime
testing_plan: Unit tests for affinity tag computation and deterministic collision checks
Simulated reconnect scenarios (drop/rejoin at various offsets) against golden transcripts to assert no tool-call boundary splits
Load test hedging under synthetic high-concurrency to measure token egress delta and CPU overhead
Fuzz tests to ensure malformed affinity headers don't crash reconstructor; such clients must fallback to conservative replay
Canary: enable hedging on 2% of traffic and monitor duplication rate and cost signals
monitoring: Alert if duplication_rate > 1% for a route after rollout
Dashboard: per-route resume_success_rate, avg_resume_latency, and functioncall_boundary_violation_count
migrations: Backward-compatible: servers without affinity support treat missing tag as unknown and fall back to current resume behavior
Client SDKs should be updated to send Last-Affinity when available; older clients still supported
Rollout plan: implement server-side support first, then ship SDKs and opt-in console toggle. Default hedging remains off until both sides present
